utterances.text: Yes, this is my reason, because the Law on the Army is being violated. Somebody who has not been authorised is now to command army troops that are headed by me. I'm the commander of the 3rd Army, and this constitutes a precedent and I was not prepared to take part in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could look at Exhibit 5D153.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a document from the following day, 13th of March, 2001, it's from the Chief of Staff, who was then General Pavkovic, and it's entitled: "Order to engage the VJ in the joint security forces of the FRY in the Republic of Serbia." And the order by Pavkovic appoints members of a coordinating body. And some of the names that we'll see in this document include witnesses that we've seen here before, General Obradovic, now and 2001 General Krzmanjelic [phoen], now-General Curkovic and this says it's based on Article 6 of the Law on the Army and an order of the 7th of March of the president of the Federal Republic. What was your -- what was your complaint about this? It appears to be in accordance with the law. It makes reference to the order signed by the president in Article 6 of the Law on the Army and the Rules of Service.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not challenging the fact that the president signed this, but what he signed is not in compliance with the law. And if you turn the page I will indicate what I as an officer understood that I could not participate in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll leave that to Mr. Bakrac, if he wants to go to that. I need to speed ahead a bit and go to the next exhibit. I think it contains part of what you want to say, that's 5D150, from the 16th of March, 2001. This is a document from you, General, to General Pavkovic personally. And it's a briefing on a meeting on the 15th, item number 2 regards the formation of the joint security and operations group forces. Now, in this don't you explain to General Pavkovic why you have a problem what's being proposed concerning these joint security forces. In item 1 you talk about the dualism in the command system.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the whole point of the problem. I was the commander of the 3rd Army and the coordinating body of the Government of Serbia, which included politicians, the police, one or two officers, were to command part of the forces of the 3rd Army. If I may be allowed to say, I asked and I went to a meeting in General Pavkovic's office where there was an entire collegium of the General Staff even before this, where I explained that Article 3 of the Law on the Army was being violated. Command can be in accordance with single command, and the coordinating body for the south of Serbia cannot be superior [Realtime transcript read in error "Serbia] to the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what happened after that meeting? Did you resign or did you continue on with the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 48, 7, the witness says "cannot be superior to this Army of Yugoslavia," and not "Serbia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, do I need to repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood your question. I still remember what you asked me. My answer is I didn't offer my resignation. This doesn't exist in the army, but I demanded, unless the Law on the Army was respected, that the president of the country replace me from my duty. He did not agree to my dismissal or my replacement. First he asked me why this was done and he signed, and the Chief of the General Staff in document later on wrote a specific proposal, the decision was changed, and the coordinating body did not command those forces, rather, the command of the 3rd Army, that is, I as the commander of the 3rd Army did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to Exhibit 5D151.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, this is the next document I found in connection with this subject and it's dated the 14th of May, 2001. It's from General Pavkovic as the Chief of Staff to President Kostunica. It's entitled: "Analysis of the latest events," talking about the joint security forces and actions that had been taken out in south Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to item number 4, which is "proposals," it's on -- I need page 3 of the English. I'm not sure where it is on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You see that, General, under number 1 the proposal is to: "Resubordinate the command of the joint security forces to the 3rd Army to avoid dual command and ... put command back within the legal framework according to the structure: President of the republic-General Staff-3rd Army command," and under the 3rd Army would be the ZSB. What does that stand for? Is that the joint security forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And command over police forces would remain with the coordinating body which comprised representatives of the VJ, police, and the joint security forces command. Who were the members of the joint security forces command? You don't have to give me names, but give me -- were they police, were they civilians, were they military? What were they?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first version it is the army and the police without civilians and civilians in the coordinating body and representatives of the police and the army. I say in the initial stage until things were restored to normal by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this body, this command that you had problems with in 2001, that was originally created on the proposal of General Pavkovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir, at whose proposal that was done. I received a summons, so to speak, from the Chief of the General Staff to set out for Belgrade one Saturday in March, for him to inform me on the spot what the president's orders were and what would happen. I then expressed my military disagreement, saying this was wrong. I asked that this president's -- this order of the president's be changed. It had already been signed. They had started to implement it, but in written form I responded and asked to be replaced from my duty for as long as that decision of the president's had not been cancelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So you don't know who proposed it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. By Their Honours leave, I can only speculate, I can guess, but -- all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to the Joint Command meetings in 1998 we saw in your testimony that nobody ever gave you an order, no civilian gave you an order during those meetings, but you don't know whether any of the civilians attending those meetings gave any orders or instructions or directions at the meetings you were not present at? You couldn't know, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know something I didn't see, something I did not receive precise information about, no, I couldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yesterday I touched on this briefly about your whereabouts on the 29th of April. We saw the document where you were in the area of Lozica village and saw the 37th Motorised Brigade. And in Exhibit P2026 we have a regular combat report of the Pristina -- of the 125th Motorised Brigade. Would you take issue with me, General, if I told you that in that report they indicate the commander and the Chief of Staff of the Pristina Corps were in the brigade from 0900 to 1200 hours today, that is, the 29th of April? We can bring up the document if you want to see it, but I don't know if you need it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's not necessary. I spoke about this yesterday. I spoke about what part of the front this happened in and if this is the report of the 125th Brigade. This refers to what I spoke about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I want to ask you a few questions about the armed non-Siptar population --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what's the actual answer to that question, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in an early answer in his direct testimony he indicated that on the 29th he had visited I think both elements of the 37th and the 125th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a small part from the 37th Brigade which I found around the village of Lozica, I happened to run into them, and went to the front line between Decani and Pec and the 125th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you give us any more precise location as to where you visited part of the 125th. You say the front line between Decani and Pec. Can you narrow it down any more for us?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first working point, so to speak, was close to Pec, the area of deployment of parts of the armoured battalion. And then east of that position part of the artillery unit for a few kilometres, and then the third point was the forward command post of that brigade in the Decani -- in the area near Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You've probably heard one of the other witnesses earlier in this case talking about a meeting of the General Staff which is in Exhibit P938 -- I'm sorry, 931 on the 2nd of February, 1999. If we could go to e-court, I need page 23 of the English and the top of page 21 in the B/C/S. And General Samardzic and General Ojdanic are talking here. General Ojdanic says: "I've heard there are 50.000 armed Serbs." General Samardzic says: "Judging by the number of weapons issued now, it's 47.000 ..." Ojdanic says: "What are the war assignments ..." And Samardzic says: "It was my order, and we organized the whole thing for the defence of Serbian villages, commanders at all levels have been sent out, they're armed and they have two combat sets of ammunition each. Their role and assignment is to defend their villages and participate together with army units in any operations in the immediate vicinity." So were you aware of this order of General Samardzic for these armed Serbs to participate with army units? Would these be some of those non-Siptar -- some of the armed non-Siptar population that we see references to in the Joint Command orders?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I saw this document was here in the courtroom, and what I know about something like this is what I saw here for the first time from this document. I don't know what General Samardzic is referring to at all. I'm a hundred per cent certain that the command of the Pristina Corps in 1998 and 1999 had neither the legal nor the de facto possibility nor was it involved in arming the civilian population. And the army commander did not have the right to issue weapons either. It was exclusively within the competence of the minister of defence. I see what it says here, but in my view it's in the sphere of the impossible. Whether he did something before that as the army commander without my knowledge, well of course I allow for the possibility. I don't know what General Samardzic did before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You gave a date there, Mr. Hannis, of the 2nd of February. That can't be the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: 2nd February 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General Samardzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, he's no longer the 3rd Army commander at that time, Your Honour, and he's a member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what was his role then? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I forget his precise title.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He is listed as the Yugoslav Army inspectorate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So are you saying the head inspector for the army did something illegal or inappropriate in connection with arming those Serbs? Or are you saying he's not telling the truth to General Ojdanic? What are you saying in your answer that he didn't have the right to issue weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that one cannot see from this text when it was done. I'm also saying that my knowledge from 1998 and 1999 says that nobody from the Pristina Corps issued a single rifle to somebody who was not a military conscript, a member of the corps. And I don't know whether General Samardzic as the army commander in 1997 and the period before that did something in connection with that. And what I know about the law is that only the Ministry of Defence can issue orders concerning the equipping, both of the army and the civil defence and all the structures in the defence system.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at Exhibit 5D175.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is an order from the Pristina Corps commander for defence. It has number 455-123. The English has the date of 6 April 1998, but that's obviously a typo because in the original even I can see that it is 1999. And we know that you weren't the commander in 1998. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 3 of both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to ask you a question about item number 2 which is entitled: "Pristina Corps task." The second paragraph says: "Task: In coordination with the Republic of Serbia MUP and other defence forces, rely on fortified ground features and populated places ..." What are the other defence forces being referred to there? Who would that be?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other defence forces are the civil defence, the civilian protection, the organs of the organization of the republics, the federal state, legal subjects, and everything envisaged by the law in this connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And two paragraphs down from that your order says: "Use armed non-Siptar population to secure military features and features of special importance for the defence of FRY, the roads - and for defence of populated places." It doesn't say anything about: Coordinate with the Ministry of Defence. It just says: Use the armed non-Siptar population, so you had the authority to do that or you apparently thought you had the authority to do that the way this is written. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. I explained during the examination-in-chief - and if I may be allowed to clarify why that's not correct - I did not think about this, either at the time or today. This is a task copied from an order issued by the commander of the 3rd Army, which I could not alter, and my understanding was that the army commander simply issued the task in harmony with his assessment, that if an opportunity should present itself, the forces of the Ministry of Defence can be engaged in the defence of the country; and if this should happen, a special order on the resubordination of specific forces would arrive. The only thing I did was reduce what I received as a task, and I did not pass it on to any other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, General, sometimes it seems you add to the task and sometimes you subtract. How do you make that decision about whether you're going to keep what you got from the 3rd Army as is or whether you're going to change it? It's a matter of your discretion, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My decision is my decision and my responsibility. As I did not receive any specific information as to what forces these were, in what locations, I did not get a list, I did not get an order on resubordination. So I simply left this out, I omitted to give such tasks to my units, and this decision was verified by the army commander who agreed with my understanding of this issue and my decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, then if you're just copying what you got from the 3rd Army, then wouldn't you agree with me that the 3rd Army commander had the authority to direct the use of the armed non-Siptar population or else he thought he did.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army commander, in view of the doctrinal principles, the Law on Defence and the Rules of Combat has the right to count on all the forces in the defence system in his area. And in those general terms, he mentions this in his decision. However, for an actual factual engagement, he did not have the authority without the resubordination of part of those forces to the army by the minister of defence. It is exclusively the minister of defence who has the power to resubordinate the forces of the civil protection and civil defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then let's go to an earlier order of yours, P2808, we've looked at this before, this is 455-1 on the 16th of February, 1999, at page 8 of the English, and there's a reference about the armed non-Siptar population.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can we scroll up. I'm having trouble finding the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this is -- General, for you, you'll see about five paragraphs up from item number 3 it says: "Later on secure the passibility of the major roads and full control of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Engage armed non-Siptars to secure military facilities and communications and to defend places with non-Siptar population." This is your order for anti-terrorist operations, and you are directing the engagement of armed non-Siptars, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Stop. You said no. Let me ask you about this. Why does it say "defend places with non-Siptar population"? You don't have concern about defending the Siptar population, do you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the pogrom, it was not the Albanian population that was threatened by the forces of the armed rebellion. That's the gist of this sentence and decision by the army commander, which I copied in the task. I cannot change it, I couldn't change it, and it is in compliance, both with the law and with military doctrine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say you couldn't change it. I thought you told us before that you sometimes added things and you sometimes left things out. So can you change it or not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't change item 2. Item 2 is a task which is to be copied, coming from the superior. In item 4, where I decide, that's where you can see whether I add or take away something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And could we look at Exhibit 3D676.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, do you want a break?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. At 5.00 I was supposed to take some medicine and I asked the guard because I know one of them has this medicine. It's not indispensable, but I think they've brought my medicine with me. They changed the guards and they didn't leave the medicine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It appears to be being attended to, Mr. Hannis, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I believe Mr. Bakrac asked you about efforts to get the Albanians in Kosovo to be a part of the defence, to be engaged in the military territorial detachments. And we've got an exhibit here which is 5D183. If we could put that up on the screen for you, it's the 10th of April, 1999. This is a document from you regarding organization and mobilisation changes. You're issuing an order, I believe it's to the Pristina Military District command to establish the 9th Military Territorial Detachment. And in item 3.1 you say: "The ... Military District Command small replenish the military territorial detachment with not yet assigned conscripts predominantly of Siptar and other ethnicities ..." And. "The commanders shall be professional military personnel of Siptar ethnicity ..." First of all, did that ever get accomplished before the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And my next question is: 3.5 says: "A report on the formation of this detachment is to be submitted to me by 5 August 1999." So it seems like this was not an urgent matter for you, General. Why such a late date for reporting on the formation -- the 5th of August turned out to be well after the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is clearly a typo if that's number 8 there. This is a third document in a row and was merely being transited via the corps commander, which is me, from the army commander to the corps, and I merely forwarded it down to the district commander. This is a mistake. If you look at the previous two documents from the army staff to the corps commander, that this is a typo. We heard the military district commander say that he was trying to implement this task during that period, but that he was unsuccessful.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I have a question about the original document on the copy I have, General. I see what appears to be a typewritten signature or at least your title and part of a stamp, but I do not -- it's been cut off when it's been copied I guess. I don't see a signature, I don't see any delivery information. How do you know that this document actually ever went out?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it because I know the events themselves. I know when I received the order from the army commander. You can see in the heading that I refer to that order and the order of the staff and the Supreme Command. And two days after resubordination I order it to the military district commander. We heard a Prosecution witness speak about that. He couldn't implement that without receiving an order from me first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, what we'll do is take the break now since the issue of medication was raised, that can be dealt with, and we can resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, yesterday we had talked about your report dated the 24th of May, 1999, about the failure regarding the resubordination of the MUP. I want to look now at Exhibit P2809, this is dated the 25th of April, 1999. I can hand you a hard copy with the assistance of the usher. And you'll see it has your signature and seal on the second page, and it is numbered 455-183. It's entitled: "Engaging MUP forces in the Pristina Corps zone." And here you make reference to the order of the 3rd Army command number 872-94/1 of 20 April 1999. One question I have, we talked yesterday about the numbering of these documents in the Pristina Corps, and we saw your original order regarding subordination of the MUP that followed on from the 3rd Army order described here has the number 455-172 along with another what I say is an unrelated document. And your 24 May 1999 report about the non-subordination of the MUP has the number 455-172/2. It seems to me it's logical, General, that this document actually should be 455-172/1, shouldn't it? Because it specifically pertains to that 3rd Army command order and that's what's referenced in your original 455-172 on this topic and what's in the 24 May report. Wouldn't you agree with me about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with the Prosecutor under the condition that at the corps command I had an entire team of people who deal with official correspondence and I would also have been -- had to have been able to follow the procedure, otherwise we see many typos and omissions, such as the one we just saw when the months were mixed up, and therefore this mix-up with the numbers is possible as well. There are many documents similar to this one, but they do not bear the 172 designation, which makes things all the more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. This document in number 1 says in the last sentence: "Other forces and institutions continued to remain under the jurisdiction of the MUP." What are you referring to there? Do you mean other groups in MUP other than the PJP and MUP territorial units? Are you referring to the SAJ, the JSO?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must confess that the Prosecutor's question is the right one to ask, since in item 1 I'm ordering something in general since I don't know what the manoeuvring units of the PJP there were or the territorial units for that matter. I didn't have their numbers, designations, and I don't know where they were at. As for the other forces, I had in mind the secretariats of the interior at the time, which had the authority to regulate law and order, the issuing of documents, and other regular tasks. I was unfortunately very imprecise in formulating this, but at the time I had no other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you had some understanding. It seems the PJP was something that should be involved in this, is that because of information you might have learned in your earlier meeting with General Pavkovic, General Djordjevic, and General Stevanovic that you told us about before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in that sense. I had some previous experience in 1998 that the manoeuvring units of the police and territorial detachments were engagement in suppressing terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. I would like to apologise, but I haven't finished my previous answer. Those units would include the SAJ under the formulation as it stands and as I was ordered. That would also include the JSO, although it is not specifically mentioned, as is the case with the SAJ. I didn't know their whereabouts at the time, I don't even know whether they were in Kosovo and Metohija. I couldn't be specific and put JSO in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Item number 2 says: "Coordinate command and defence and other combat operations at the level of the ZJT," which is translated here as combined tactical units, "and in keeping with the already-issued decisions and the plan of engagement of combined contingents." Has this plan of engagement of combined contingents been a document that's been exhibited here? Is that one that we've seen earlier in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In addition to the order there was a plan per brigade zones, stating where -- which of the brigades should locate a police unit and establish contact. This joining at the beginning refers to other plans and operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... engagement drafted, written up?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this order was being drafted in attachment number 2 to this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Item number 3 says: "Include the new military territorial detachments and armed civilians." Which armed civilians are you referring to here in item 3?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Serbian text it says "armed population in the zone." You go back to the initial story, or rather, the initial order of Grom 3, the civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. I have a question regarding item number 4. It talks about military conscripts from RJ. What does RJ stand for? It's translated here with a question mark as "reserve units."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In a war all units at the level of regiment and brigade are called "ratne jedinice," war unit, and then we have lower-ranking units. RJs begin with the level of brigade, this is a general term.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are those war units VJ units or military territorial detachments? What are those war units? To whom do they pertain?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that the war units were part of the VJ, but war units were also the military territorial detachments. This is imprecise. Military territorial units are also VJ and RJs certainly are as well, those are the brigades I referred to. Military territorial units were part of the military districts of Pristina or Nis, which is outside Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It says here that you should take those who have been temporarily engaged in MUP reserve units by a separate order dating from 1998. So these are individuals who have been in the MUP reserve and now you're directing that they be brought into the army in the war units, correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My precise answer would be that a part of the military conscripts from the war units of the army was engaged, or rather, included into performing police tasks, be -- by them being transferred to the police service without the military defence offices knowing or by being temporarily transferred to the police units. But military districts cannot do that on their own. They all had to be returned to the army as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what the separate order dating back from 1998 was and who had issued that order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly cannot be precise at this moment as to what order exactly it was. I remember that an order was signed by the Chief of Staff of the army, General Simic, he appeared here as witness. And in mid-1998 as the Chief of Staff, he warned the military district of Pristina on the need to deal with the problem of any military conscripts from the army that are part of police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The commander of the Pristina Military District at this time in April 1999, was that Colonel Pesic who testified here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did he comply with this order forthwith, as directed in item 4? Did he manage to get those conscripts back from MUP reserve units and into VJ war units?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that the deadline set here was unrealistic, but it all points to the fact that this task was a very serious one to implement, since we had problems with replenishing the Pristina Corps. The entire military administrative procedure had to be resolved, the issues therein, that is. As to whether he managed to carry out this task completely, I truly don't know. Work was being done, there are reports in existence, but I don't know what the figure was. I knew that some people were outside war units and I demanded that it be dealt with ASAP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Maybe I've oversimplified here, but this seems sort of analogous to what we were talking about at the start of the day when MUP had equipment loaned to it by the VJ and you don't know if or when the army got it back. And here it seems like you have personnel that have sort of been loaned to the MUP and you don't know whether or when you got it all back, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no loans. You cannot loan a human being. The issue at hand is that the military territorial organs did not have proper records, and there are such documents in existence from which you can deduce how many Pristina Corps members were outside their home units. I truly cannot remember now, but I believe that was also admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I waited for the witness to complete his answer. My learned friend Mr. Hannis said two hours, and that was his calculation as of last night so as to equal that to the length of examination-in-chief, but we are now past three hours of his cross-examination. I don't know whether any limits have been set or whether Mr. Hannis may go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now would certainly not be the moment to interrupt him; however, if you are going to significantly exceed what we would normally expect you to confine cross-examination to, you should really justify it, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm fully intending to end before the end of the day, and I know I have exceeded two hours but there were a lot of interruptions and translation issues, et cetera. If I may ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In view of the importance of the witness and the evidence, we consider it appropriate that you should be allowed to continue on the basis that you suggest, that is, that you're likely to finish by the end of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page of this document in both --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do that. Can I ask you, Mr. Lazarevic, I maybe don't fully understand this document, but was this issued in the context of your serious efforts to implement the resubordination order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, this was trying to put things into practice pertaining to the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And in paragraph 1 it refers to engaging the PJP and MUP territorial units, and then it goes on to refer to other forces and institutions. So the first part of this is a clear statement that you envisage your subordinates endeavouring to take command of the PJP and the MUP territorial units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. Territorial units of the MUP are also detachments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you also envisaged them taking control of the armed civilians, that's the civil defence as you've described it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not quite. I'm asking them to include within the system of control of territory those units. This would understand combined efforts in keeping with the Law on Defence to use all defence elements. Control includes command, which can take place only provided resubordination was ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go to page 2 of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, at the bottom we see it says: "Sent to all subordinate commands, the VoK Pristina command and the MUP staff." We don't see any kind of delivery information as we've seen on some of the other documents. Do you know why that is?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information on who the document was delivered to -- well, you can only see that on the telegram, if it went through the station for encryption. This was sent by couriers rather than through the encryption service.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Above your signature line we see enclosed, number 1, "locations of MUP detachments in the zone of the brigade on a map." Where did you obtain your information about where the MUP detachments were located? Who had given that to you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operative organ of the corps command tried to have a map to accompany this order. They tried to do that via brigade commands or contacting directly some of SUP chiefs by whatever means they had at their disposal. I remember that the map was attachment number 1 and 2. We tried to locate those brigades with the use of that map so that we could contact them more easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... several individuals in the MUP in order to create the map?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's how the operations officer got this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And enclosed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That question was incomplete because of overlap. What was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- did you obtain that information from several different individuals in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, it's been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Number 2 enclosed is: "Plan of engagement of the joint units with their activities and task." [Realtime transcript read in error "staff"] . From what I've read above, General, it sounds like is this some sort of blank form or table to be filled in or was this a plan where you already had listed task?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, it's a pity that it is not now attached to this document, but I remember the text part where the brigades are listed as joint units, as joint tactical units, and in the right -- on the right-hand side of that sheet it was a landscape paper. It says: Tasks, combat control of the territory, and then it says also whether a brigade is deployed in the border belt. So you have in a text form all the tasks of that brigade, and also it is specified how those tasks can be carried out, primarily to achieve combat control of the territory. There are five or six tasks, if I remember correctly, they're all listed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So had you or somebody in the Pristina Corps command already filled in that information on this plan that was attached to this document when it was sent out?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is not a specific plan that is related to any combat action. This is just an instruction of sorts, how those brigades should combine those operations or activities within their areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If we could look just briefly at the transcript line 23 on page 68, it should be tasks and not staff, that's the last word in that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, that's my slur probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, we talked before about your 24th May 1999 report about the failure of MUP subordination. You told us at page 18237 on the 14th of November that "the immediate reason for me to report to the commander of the army about this in writing is the oral and written report of the commander of the 37th Motorised Brigade." I think I had asked you before if we had seen that document in evidence so far, and I don't believe we have. I've looked for documents from Colonel Dikovic that might talk about that around that time, and I will tell you that I've only been able to find two that speak to MUP forces other than the one we looked at regarding the elephant to kill a fly comment. On the 25th of April in Exhibit 5D1088 we have a report and proposal from Colonel Dikovic, if we could put that on the screen for you, and we'll need to go to page 2 of the English and scroll to the bottom of the B/C/S. In item number 2 Dikovic says: "With regard to engaging MUP forces in the zone of responsibility, we think and propose to engage the main forces of the MUP and combat monitoring and control of the territory in the flanks of the zone ..." And I'm skipping to the next paragraph. "By the same token, we think that the engagement of the MUP organs (particularly the units of variant II) so far has been inappropriate and inadequate relative to the strength of their forces (there are about 600 members of the MUP in the zone of responsibility of the Brigade). The reason for this is that at the check-points where they are located they secure only themselves and not the territory and they have been appropriately called squatters ..." Is this the report that caused you to write your 24 May complaint or report to General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a report from a brigade commander relative to the previous document that I authored. He received my order, my map, and the engagement plan. He carries out this order, he complies with it; and in his combat report, he proposes how those forces should be involved, should be engaged. So this has nothing to do with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The only other reference I was able to find from the 37th is document 5D1085, if we could put that up. And, General, this is a 13 May 1999 regular combat report closer in time to your report. It's to the Pristina Corps command from the 37th, Colonel Dikovic, and under item 2.1 he mentions an action in Ovcarevo, and Obrinje being re-planned and to coordinate with Colonel Stefanovic from Pristina Corps command, representatives of the 122nd Detachment of the PJP, someone from the artillery group and representatives of the 7th Infantry Brigade were briefed on the plan, et cetera, and there's no complaint here about the MUP. So that could not have been what triggered your writing a report on the 24th. Is there any more specific information you can tell us about when you got a written report from him about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to be quite specific yesterday in the time between the 20th and the 23rd of April. I'd rather say that it was between the 20th and the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please clarify the date. It is not clear now whether he is referring to March or the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Let me back up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say it was between the 20th and the 23rd of April that you had the disturbing report from Colonel Dikovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, it's May. I have to apologise if I said "April."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... In your report the 24th of May, you talk about MUP tolerating criminal activities undertaken by its members against the Siptar civilian population: Murder, rape, looting, robbery, aggravated theft. Now, I want to relate that to something that you had told us about before concerning the problems in the 175th Brigade that you told us a little bit about. You and General Pavkovic had gone on an inspection tour around the beginning of May. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I think it was the 1st or the 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And eventually that commander was removed from his position, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was removed from his position as the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like you to look at Exhibit 5D382 for a moment. This is a 27 April 1999 official note from Major Miroslav Panic. Did you see this document before today? Did you see it when you were preparing to testify?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At the end on page 2 of both the English and B/C/S he explains -- he has explained part of what he has done to investigate some of the allegations against the commander and others and concludes that he believes there are no grounds to dismiss the commander. Do you see that at the very end?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did anything happen to Major Panic at or around the time that the commander of the 175th was replaced? Was he replaced as well, do you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. He was also replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In item 5 up above his signature he talks about the 26th of April where the security organ of the 175th detained a couple of individuals who had set a house on fire, a house belonging to an unidentified Siptar, and those guys had been wearing camouflage uniforms and carrying automatic rifles and had introduced themselves as volunteers from the 175th Brigade. It says even though they were from the village of Klokot they will be handed over to the investigating judge on the next day. Do you know anything about that particular case? Were those two individuals volunteers from the 175th?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those were not volunteers. Those were locals, those two, and there are four others who are listed here, civilians. They were arrested by the army after they were found in the commission of those acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... camouflage uniforms and carrying the automatic rifles, how did you find out that they were civilians or are you basing that just on what you read here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what it says literally here, but I know that the security organ of the corps dealt with that, dealt with all those issues in Kosovsko Pomoravlje this phenomenon, those civilians who were roaming around committing those crimes and wherever possible the army dealt with those problems together with the SUP in Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well from what we've seen in other documents and what we've heard about the number of weapons that were allegedly issued, could these two guys be part of the armed non-Siptar population? Those are Serb names, aren't they, they're not Siptars?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, they would be ethnic Serbs based on this, but for somebody to be a member of the armed non-Siptar population, that actually referred to the civilian protection, civil defence. And as for these two, I can't tell whether they were members of those structures. But at any rate, they did not conduct themselves in accordance with the rules for members of the civil defence as civil defence members were supposed to comport themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... so from what we read from this they were not members of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But it appears they were arrested or detained by the VJ, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were at -- they were stopped at the check-point and -- because they were wearing some sort of uniform and they were misrepresenting themselves. When they were questioned by the authorised organs, they were police officers who were there at that check-point and they have the power to carry out those preliminary investigative actions, they arrested them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... says the security organ of the 175th brought into detention these two guys. There's no mention of a check-point, there's no mention of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we go back to the beginning of this official note, it -- the check-point in Klokot is mentioned. And in this very sentence here, the last-but-one, this check-point in the village of Klokot is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for clearing up the sake of confusion I believe the evidence is talking about military police, which are obviously not part of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, does that assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's right, isn't it, General, you're talking about military police, not MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. In one context I mentioned there were other reports where the military police organs and the MUP in that area tried to prevent those civilians, those locals or whoever that was, from committing crimes. There are such reports from brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, but, General, there's nothing in this nothing document that suggests anything but it being the VJ, in particular the security organ, that brought these two individuals into custody, into detention, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the procedure for -- whereby those people were stopped at the check-point in the village of Klokot, and item 3 at the very end, towards the end, this is mentioned there. And the first on front page we can see that. So they were stopped at the check-point, and then the security organ took them in for questioning, whatever the procedure is, and they were handed over to the investigative organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, that's item 3, and item 4 is talking about information about alleged rape cases, and item 5 is something different, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to item 5, I'm sorry, yes, item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And in the last part of item 5, it says the same day four named individuals were brought into detention by the military police for having looted abandoned Siptar houses. So here the military police are arresting civilians for having looted civilian houses, Siptar houses, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could look at Exhibit 5D991 I have a couple of questions on that, General. This is a 13 May 1999 document from the I think the military district command. It's an interim combat report to the command of the Pristina Corps. I want to look at paragraph 3 and it talks about an incident in which a member of the military territorial detachment was wounded apparently in the course of a discussion or an altercation with someone who's described as a drunk MUP member. And it says that MUP member was taken into custody and handed over to the MUP organs. I gather then that someone from either the military territorial detachment or from the VJ are the ones who took him into custody?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police within the military district brought in this police officer, who was drunk and he caused this incident, and handed him over to the police organs. And they also arrested the civilian who had been torching houses and he was also handed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the last paragraph we see a reference that members of the military territorial detachment arrested a civilian, it looks like a Serb civilian, who had been setting houses on fire. And it indicates he will be turned over to the MUP organs and a criminal report will be filed by the military police, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So from these two documents it appears that the military police can arrest civilians who commit crimes against the Siptar civilians, such as looting their houses. It also appears that they can arrest a MUP individual, in this case he committed a crime against a military territorial detachment individual, but it looks like they have the power to at least detain and arrest those people. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there can be no dilemma. If someone attacks a member of the military, that person would be arrested regardless of who they are. That's quite natural and normal. As for the thing at the end, members of the military territorial detachment arrested a citizen. It is not -- it doesn't say here that the military police arrested this man. Those were members of a unit who saw civilian committing a crime, and they performed a citizen's arrest in a way, so to speak. The unit does not have the right to arrest the detachment, 180th detachment. It doesn't say here that the military police arrested him. He was caught, so to speak, by those people, and he was handed over to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The security organs that arrested those individuals in the last document we looked at for burning Siptar houses or looting Siptar houses, was that also a couple of examples of citizen's arrest by military police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Then my question to you is if that could be done and indeed was done at least on these two instances, why wasn't it done if army members were on notice and aware that MUP members were committing murder, rape, robbery, theft against Siptar, Albanian, civilians? Why wasn't that done?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see two things from this. One thing is when a person is found in the commission of a crime, then every citizen may act in accordance with the law and need to either report or not. The military did what it did, it operated in its own way. And the second thing is if you get some information, to check something. And according to the report in this specific case, the report that I sent to the army commander, the security organ went out to check all this information, both within the brigade and also from the department of the interior in Glogovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where do you see that the security organ went out to check out all that information in your report? Is there a security organ report about that investigation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I started saying that in my examination-in-chief and then I was interrupted. I was told not to say what was done in accordance with this report, and I am telling you that three teams headed out on three issues: The resubordination had not been completed yet, the clear-up [as interpreted] operations, and the information about alleged crimes by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And my question is: Is there some report reflecting that the security organ went out to investigate those alleged crimes by the police? Is that a document that's been shown in this case in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was not shown. I hope that we will soon be able to hear first-hand from the people who were dealing with that and who were actually acting on the order to check this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, it might not be a big issue, but 17 -- 78, 15, the witness said the "assanation" not the clean-up operations, because we've been hearing "assanation" for some time, so -- it's 78, 15. So they went for three different tasks, one was resubordination has not been completed; the "assanation" of the battle-field, and the information about the alleged crimes of the police. That's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the difference between that and clearing up?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't wondering if that doesn't sort of suggesting something different than "assanation" because we have been using "assanation" throughout the whole trial, that's the only reason why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I ask you these questions because you've told us and we see many of your documents to support your position to show how concerned you were about caring for the civilians during this conflict, and I say to you, sir, that all those orders and all those words are all very good and well, but when it came down to really helping those civilians, when you had information that they were the -- being the victims of crimes, serious crimes, murder, rape, robbery, by MUP individuals, it doesn't look like you did very much. You wrote this one-page vague report with some wide-sweeping allegations, send it to Pavkovic -- or handed it to Pavkovic, he was that close to you, and you didn't do anything else. Do you really think that shows your desire to take good care of the civilians, particularly the Siptar civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the report I did not get information that was specific enough, that is why the report is the way it is, but that's why I sent three teams out into the field to deal with those problems. And I actually make a claim that is completely contrary to what Mr. Prosecutor is putting to me, that to the best of our abilities, as much as it was possible in the chaos of war, we did everything we could to assist the civilian population in Kosovo and Metohija. We provided protection, medical treatment, rescue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, General. The last thing I want to ask you about is the plan or no plan on the 12th of November in response to a question from Mr. Bakrac at page 18129, line 6, you said: "Before this Trial Chamber, speaking under an oath, as I have been for several days now, I can categorically state that there was no plan that the corps command or its subordinate units knew of or participated in or got from their superiors, so absolutely not." I note that you specifically said there was no plan that the corps command or its subordinate units knew of. It seems to me, sir, that allows for the possibility that there may have been a plan known of by others higher than you. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian language is what it is. The Prosecutor has made use of the expression I used, so perhaps my imprecise way of expressing myself, but I have to repeat that really and truly I neither heard of the existence of any plan nor did I see or learn about it at any level. In the wartime chaos, as the Prosecutor is suggesting, that level was far away from us. And if I may be permitted to say so, I'm convinced that at no level was it possible for such a plan to exist from the aspect of my understanding of the defence of the country at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that at the very beginning of the war, the 24th of March, 1999, the intelligence that the army had was that you did not genuinely expect a land invasion by NATO forces for some period of time, perhaps for at least a couple of weeks. You knew enough about the situation to know that they probably wouldn't be able to mount such a massive undertaking for some short period of time, two weeks, maybe a little longer. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents from the relevant period which have been seen in this courtroom indicate that it wasn't quite like that, and that in our assessment we believed that by the 5th of April, at the latest, a ground operation would be launched. So at the end of March I already ordered the closure of all axes and a total defence, and we showed that here, defence from total aggression. That was my understanding of the problem in late March and the threat of a ground operation and we have shown documents about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we talk about the 5th of April, we're talking about maybe 12 days. Some window of opportunity, if you will, General, between the beginning of the bombing and when you might expect a ground invasion, and we heard the evidence from Witness K-73 who is the fellow that you and I talked about before who gave you a heel click and a nod before he left the courtroom and he told us about hearing from General Pavkovic shortly before the bombs started falling that once that happened and there's some dispute about exactly what the wording was I think in his statement, he said that Pavkovic said, First thing we need to do is get the Albanian from our back. I think on cross-examination he said he wasn't sure whether it was get the Albanian from our back or get the KLA from our back. But isn't that true in those first days, week and a half, 10, 12 days, that the focus of the Pristina Corps was on routing and destroying as much of the Siptar terrorist forces of the KLA as they possibly could? Wasn't that one of your primary focuses during those first days?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My best reply as regards that activity was that at that time only 4 to 5 per cent of the overall manpower of the corps was engaged for that activity. The rest were defending the border, and that is the best indicator of where the focus of defence was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I respectfully have to disagree with you. I think the documents in the evidence from the other individuals, I would include Exhibit P1990, which is a MUP meeting on the 17th of February, where it's talked about this window of opportunity before a ground invasion happens. And your main effort was to try to get rid of as many of those guys as possible so that you could use all your other resources to fight NATO when the expected land invasion came. And as part of routing and destroying those Siptar terrorist forces, that included getting rid of their support base, burning houses and driving out the civilians that provided them food and logistics and shelter. Isn't that right, that's what happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, General. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Now, there was an earlier indication of a desire to further cross-examine the accused. Mr. Visnjic, your basis for doing that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I tried to find an appropriate term. My -- I thank you for giving me the floor. My basis is the examination of my colleague Mr. Ackerman, in the course of which he put some matters to the witness which the witness did not mention during Mr. Bakrac's examination-in-chief. When I tried to raise the issue, my colleague Mr. Ackerman gave me to understand how he saw the rule that had been introduced. So if you will allow me to respond to that. The impression has been gained from what my colleague Mr. Ackerman said here, that I deliberately waived the right to my, or rather, set aside my right to cross-examination in order to follow his cross-examination, thus changing the order. Firstly, as I understand the right to cross-examination, this is my right to check every new circumstance that appears in the courtroom in the best interests of my client. In this case, where we have several accused, the cross-examination can sometimes relate not to checking what the witness has said but getting additional information from the witness when a certain defence case is being presented. I'll give you a typical example of this. For example, if I decide in my Defence case not to call a single witness, knowing there will be other witnesses called after my Defence where I will be able to put my case. In that case, my colleague, Mr. Fila, would never have the chance to check what I was trying to show through those witnesses. Because if this rule is accepted as absolute, the rule would not allow him to follow me and check certain statements. In this particular case, the question of anticipation has been raised, Mr. Fila's anticipation as to whether, based on the list of evidence I present, what questions I will put, and what line of defence I will try to present through those witnesses. We have two additional problems here, one is the time needed for that kind of anticipation, and you will see that in the case of ordinary witnesses whose testimony is very brief, unlike that of General Lazarevic here, we get information about the evidence at the time they make the solemn declaration. If they are examined for an hour or two, my colleague Mr. Fila must be ready right away to deal with a huge number of exhibits, to peruse them, and to establish precisely what the case put by each of us, including the Prosecutor, will be. In this particular case, the testimony of General Lazarevic, my colleague Mr. Ackerman announced 59 documents in a mail of the 6th of November, 2007. However, on the morning, the very morning, when he started his cross-examination he withdrew that mail. And in another mail of 11th of November, 2007, which was sent at 8.00 p.m., and which I only saw on the 12th of November in the morning, he stated a completely different list containing some dozen documents or so. During his cross-examination of the witness he asked him about two documents that I wished to cross-examine the witness about. The first of these is P1459, that's a document which had not [as interpreted] been placed on the first list provided by Mr. Ackerman, and therefore I was unable to prepare for that document. The second document is P1725, which is a document which was actually on the list, it's a letter from General Pavkovic to the Supreme Command Staff dated the 4th of June, 1999. And I wish to demonstrate that this latter document is a typical example of the kind of problems we run into when the Defences follow one another. This document, P1725, has not been checked through a single witness of the Pavkovic Defence. On the 26th of October, 2007, on pages 17663 and 17666, we cross-examined a witness of the Pavkovic Defence, General Stojmirovic in connection with this document, it was done by my colleague Mr. Sepenuk, attempting, since he was a person who was one signatories of this document, to get some information from him. Now, we have a document which is now being put to General Lazarevic, who is asked to comment on it. Your Honours, I think it's my right in connection with document 1725 to cross-examine the witness, and especially in connection with document P1459, which was not announced on the list for my colleague Mr. Ackerman's cross-examination. Both documents have been mentioned, they were mentioned on the transcript of the 13th of November, 2007, pages 18173 to 18178. It's an entire set of questions concerning the reporting of the 3rd Army to the Supreme Command Staff on information relating to the non-resubordination of the MUP and the control or inspection that the Supreme Command Staff carried out at the time in the units of the Pristina Corps. I've spoken at some length, but I wanted to make use of this time at the end of the day and I hope I have not exhausted the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: P1459 was intimated at some stage, was it, that was on --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, and withdrawn that very morning when the witness was supposed to answer the cross-examination of my colleague Mr. Ackerman and myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I've perhaps not followed this accurately. The -- 1459 you said was not on the first list?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, it was on the first list but not the second, which cancelled out the first one. The second list was dated the 11th of November at 8.00 in the evening. The first list was on the 6th of November, I don't have the time here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 1459 was not on the first list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 1459 was on the first list of the 6th of November, 2007 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The translation at 85, 1, that it was not on the first list --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it was on the first list. So I now don't have a clear picture of the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what happened to it after that? You knew about it all along, right. And 1725 was on the list is the translation here as well, 85, lines 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll try to be precise. There is the first list which was sent on the 6th of November, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second list was sent on the 11th November, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but when did P -- when was P1725 first referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1725 is on both lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And P1459 was not on the second list?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct and the second list begins with the words: "Please disregard the previous e-mail sent regarding the documents for use by the Pavkovic Defence team -- [In English] We intend to use the following documents during the cross-examination [Interpretation] and then there follows the list including that document, P1725.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On what day was the cross-examination by Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I was meant to start on the 12th. The mail was sent on the 11th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It must have been the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he started on the 12th and continued on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So by the time P1459 was referred to, it was not on an active list of exhibits that would be used in the Ackerman cross-examination; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. And your motion is confined to this issue of -- that's -- that involves these two exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour, and that's what I would like to ask the witness about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what is it that was asked that you say requires further examination by you? Is it just quite simply the suggestion contained in these or which may be supported by these that information was being submitted to the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness was asked about P1459, he was asked whether he was familiar with those documents, or rather, that document. And I would like to elaborate further. I would like to find out more about what the witness knows about the document, it's on page 18177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can only justify that at this stage if something has occurred since you had your opportunity to cross-examine which requires you to deal with; in other words, the case against you has somehow or other been strengthened. Because these exhibits are known to you, whether Ackerman intends to ask questions about them or not, and if your decision at your turn is to take -- to ask no questions about them, then that's it unless something had subsequently happened that prejudices your position in some way. Now, what is it that happened to prejudice your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I have been prejudiced because the witness confirmed first that he knew about this document, and I believe that it is my right to ask him further questions about the following: When did he see in document first, in which circumstances he saw this document first, who showed him that document, and some other questions related to the questions -- the answers that will be given to the previous questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Aleksic, what do you wish to say on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I find myself in an unenviable position, but I will answer my learned friend Mr. Visnjic. First, as regards the second exhibit, P1725, that Mr. Visnjic said was not admitted into evidence, he is not correct in this regard -- yes, well, if it is -- well, it was admitted into evidence on the 5th of October, and it's a different story as to what was happening with this document. As regards the first document, I would agree with you that this document is well-known to all of us, and I believe that from the cross-examination by my colleague Mr. Ackerman there were no new facts that arose from his cross-examination. And the question in the examination of some of Ojdanic's defence witnesses was whether it was received by the General Staff. The question was not how this document was drafted. And I don't believe that the witness answered any of the questions in this regard. So I don't think that there were any new things that arose from the cross-examination, any new information that arose from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do I take it from that submission that you oppose Mr. Visnjic's motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am co-counsel and I have to follow the instructions of my lead counsel, and he's absent at the moment. Yes, I do oppose it, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Hannis, is there anything on this you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, you seem anxious to say some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, sometimes it is very difficult to anticipate, even if you have a document on the list you don't know what the witness would say with regard to that document. I could now give you an example used by Mr. Hannis today regarding the alleged air-strikes on schools. From that question that he asked, the witness could have given ten different answers to that question. And now if you think that we should be able to anticipate all those answers, I think that given the time restraints and the number of documents that we have in front of us, I believe that this is really quite difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: With respect, Mr. Visnjic, I think you're misinterpreting what I said to you. What I said to you is that your right to further cross-examine arises where something occurs after you have finished that prejudices your position and that you cannot be expected to have foreseen. And there might even be situations in which the latter part of that is not required, but here the documents in question are exhibited and the issue for us is whether something occurred after you made your decision not to cross that prejudices your position. And we shall have to reflect on that and make a decision. Now, is there anything else you want to say before we complete this?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well a very simple reply. I could not have known that General Lazarevic would confirm whether he was aware of that document or not. This is something that I could not have anticipated at the moment when Mr. Ackerman asked that. For the document P1459 that was not announced at all or for the document P1725 which even a witness testifying in Mr. Pavkovic's Defence was not able to confirm that he remembered that document at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying that Mr. Lazarevic said that he was aware of P1725?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he was asked questions, questions about this document at pages 1874 [as interpreted] through 1877 [as interpreted] and he made certain comments about this document.
