I would have to now find the specific reference to see whether he made those comments on the basis of any knowledge that he obtained about this document later or whether he had contemporaneous insight into this document, whether he had seen the document at the time, at the relevant time. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The only note I have is that he said that it reflected what had been said in Velickovic's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour, but there is a series of events between Velickovic's report and the issuance of this document that I would like to question the General on, and there are two documents issued by the General Staff that are related to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you see the problem already, don't you, that no doubt Mr. Ackerman will want to deal with the two documents that you decide to introduce?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are exhibits, they have already been exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if they're already exhibits, they're already there and you're not prejudiced.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but one of those pertains directly to an order issued by the 3rd Army to General Lazarevic, and I want General Lazarevic to confirm that he had received it or had not received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you'll have to identify these to me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these are 3D694 and 3D700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll tell you the outcome of this tomorrow morning. Mr. Bakrac, do you have any idea how long your re-examination will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to go through the examination today to see whether there is any re-examination arising from that, but I hope that I will be able to complete my re-examination in the first two sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, General, at this late hour I'm causing problems for everybody, but very little question about -- there's just a little clarification I'm seeking from you. What is the role of the inspector, General, in the army, because I thought it had to deal mainly with discipline. Do you defer with this, this understanding which I have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not agree with you. It is a far broader authority that the inspection of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia has. It has the right and duty to monitor, control, inspect every element of combat-readiness, from command to logistics. And discipline is just a small segment of command. So command, mobilisation, security, morale, logistics, there is inspection of every element according to certain rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: But it's merely inspection and report on the readiness of the army and the way things were being done on that account, nothing more, is it? I mean, like as a corps commander you could go for combat, but they couldn't order anything like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They could not issue orders, but their assessment of the overall combat-readiness predominated in the assessment of the combat-readiness of a unit, that was the only aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm very grateful you've educated me on this, but tell me whether General Samardzic, when General Samardzic was the inspector general, which period, and this is my last question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my recollection, after the 15th of January, 1999, and throughout that period when he handed over his duty as commander of the 3rd Army to the new commander General Pavkovic, the 15th of January, 1999, onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: For how long about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't reply with precision, throughout all of 1999 at least. As for 2000, I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, thank you to everyone for their patience allowing us to hear these additional submissions and that additional question. We shall resume tomorrow at 9.00 rather than the previously anticipated 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
